subject: Renewal: proposal for increased hosted API commit + soft-burst offer
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@fastretail.co>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>; lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-05-05 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — looking at a meaningful commit increase

Hi Soojin / Lauren,

Thanks again for the convo this morning. As we discussed with product, our usage across the recommendation and search flows has grown faster than projected — we see a 2.6x month-over-month uptick for the last quarter.

We'd like to move from our current hosted monthly commit of 1.2M tokens to 3.5M tokens effective June 1, 2025. Key asks:
- Confirm per-token rate tiers for the new band and whether the existing soft-burst pocket can be increased in the first 90 days.
- Can we keep the same latency SLA for the primary model (rwd-open-13b) if we move to the higher commit?
- Any impact to rate limits per-second or concurrent requests we should plan for?

I've attached a quick usage export and a one-pager from Eng outlining peak QPS patterns. Marco (cc) will own ops coordination.

We want to get an amendment in place next week so finance can calendar the higher billing starting June.

Best,
Alicia Gomez
Head of AI Product
FastRetail Inc.

[attachment: FastRetail_usage_May2025.csv]

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@fastretail.co>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>; karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-05-05 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — looking at a meaningful commit increase

Alicia — thanks for the details and the export, helpful. Congrats on the growth. Short answers up front, more below:

- Per-token rate: we can move FastRetail to the 3M-5M monthly commit band; the blended per-token rate for that band is $0.0009/token for generation and $0.00035/token for embeddings for the first 12 months (we can discuss a stepped scale after year 1).
- Soft-burst: we can increase the short-term burst pocket from 15% to 30% for the first 90 days to accommodate onboarding spikes; we'll log usage so this can be re-evaluated.
- Latency SLA: model and region parity maintained — no SLA change on the primary model in hosted AP-south region with this commit increase. If you plan to pin a quantized variant later, we should run perf validation.
- Rate limits: default per-account RPS will increase from 60 rps to 140 rps; concurrent request slots will be bumped from 20 -> 40. If your traffic shape has large burst windows, we recommend enabling continuous batching and KV-prefix caching (ops can help).

Next steps I propose:
1) I will circulate an amendment reflecting the new monthly commit (3.5M), the 30% 90-day soft-burst, updated rate limits, and the blended rates.
2) Karthik — can you confirm capacity pre-provisioning and whether we need to schedule a canary rollout for the larger traffic on May 29?
3) Alicia/Marco — if you confirm, we'll send a DocuSign amendment and target invoice effective June 1.

I'll attach a draft amendment and a summary sheet.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0122

[attachment: proposed-amendment-FR-2025.pdf]

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>; lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia@fastretail.co>; Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@fastretail.co>
Date: 2025-05-06 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — looking at a meaningful commit increase

Looping in ops details. TL;DR — we can provision, but need FastRetail to confirm traffic shape and whether model variants change. Notes: 

- Capacity: We can pre-allocate additional GPU instances to meet the new committed baseline (estimate: +4 T4-equivalent workers for hosted cluster in us-west-2) by May 28.
- Canary: recommend a two-phase canary: 10% traffic May 29–31, 50% June 1–3, full roll June 5. We will monitor tail latency and 99th percentile.
- Rate limits: increasing the RPS ceiling to 140 is fine; if you intend to add webhook-based streaming or server-initiated pushes we should raise concurrent slots further (request that in the next 48h).
- Caching: suggest enabling prefix-level KV caching for search request IDs — should cut token costs on repetitive prefixes by ~18%.
- Instrumentation: we need a short-term tracing hook (X-Trace-ID header) added to requests so we can correlate spikes to latencies during the canary.

I'll schedule a 30-minute ops runbook sync with Marco on May 20 — invite to follow.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Technical Program Manager, Serving Runtime
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

[inline: summary of provisioning estimates]

From: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@fastretail.co>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>; soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>; Alicia Gomez <alicia@fastretail.co>
Date: 2025-05-07 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — looking at a meaningful commit increase

Thanks everyone — confirms the plan from our side. Quick items: 

- We accept the 3.5M monthly commit and the blended rates as listed. Finance has approved the billing change to hit June 1. Please send the amended agreement (DocuSign) and the updated invoice cadence.
- We'll enable X-Trace-ID by May 25 and will share a short sample of traffic shape (CSV) by EOD May 9.
- Agree to the canary cadence; we'll throttle upstream traffic to hold to 10% during the first window.

Request: can Redwood add a one-time onboarding credit equal to 5% of the June invoice to help cover engineering validation costs? If possible we can sign this week.

If you can send DocuSign today with the amendment and the credit line included, we'll route for signature and have it back by Friday.

Thanks — Marco
VP Engineering, FastRetail Inc.
